settings.heading: Who is this for?
settings.content:
• Bunions (hallux valgus)
  • Pain and pressure at the big-toe joint
  • A red, swollen bump on the side of the foot
  • A big toe that drifts toward the other toes
  • Pain in narrow or tight shoes

settings.heading: How to use
settings.content:
EMS muscle training. Wrap the corrector around your forefoot and fasten the strap so it's snug but comfortable. Slip the soft loop over your big toe so it's guided into a straighter line. Switch it on and raise the level until you feel a gentle tingling contraction, never pain. Relax for 15 minutes, hands free.

Alignment frame. For the whole session the frame holds your big toe toward its natural line, taking pressure off the swollen joint.

settings.heading: Who shouldn't use it?
settings.content: Don't use EMS if you have a pacemaker or other implanted device, are pregnant, have epilepsy, or have broken or irritated skin on the foot. If you have diabetes, circulation problems or a diagnosed foot condition, check with your doctor or podiatrist first.

settings.eyebrow: Ease your bunion at the source
settings.heading: Calm bunion pain at home, in just [15 minutes a day]
settings.text:
Years of walking, narrow shoes and muscle imbalance slowly pull the big toe out of line. The joint drifts, the bump grows, and every step lands on the same sore, inflamed spot.

Here's the part most people never hear about.

It isn't only the bone. Along the inside of your foot runs a small muscle, the abductor hallucis, whose job is to pull your big toe away from the others and hold it straight. As the toe drifts, that muscle goes slack and quiet. Once it stops doing its job, the toe keeps sliding.

Blomar's alignment frame eases your big toe back toward its natural line, lifting pressure off the joint so the swelling and throbbing can calm down. Meanwhile EMS pulses activate the abductor hallucis for you, the muscle you can't switch on by yourself, helping it learn to hold your toe where it belongs.

settings.heading: Fix your bunion at [the source]
settings.text:
Bunion surgery is costly, means weeks off your feet, and the recovery puts most people off for years. So they try the cheap options first, silicone spacers and stiff night splints, and keep hitting the same wall.

The moment those come off, the toe drifts back, because a toe that's held isn't a toe that's trained. Passive supports can even let the muscle weaken further.

Blomar gives you the mechanical alignment that eases pressure and gives the joint room to breathe, and the EMS adds the active muscle work on the abductor hallucis, the exact muscle that keeps your big toe in line.

settings.image_alt: Wearing the corrector on the sofa
settings.heading: Teaches your toe to [hold itself straight]
settings.text:
Night splints and toe spacers share the same flaw: the second you take them off, nothing holds your toe except the same weak muscle that let it drift in the first place.

Blomar's EMS trains that muscle to do the holding itself. Repeated, gentle contractions rebuild the connection between nerve and muscle and strengthen the abductor hallucis,

so it kicks in during everyday standing and walking, keeping your big toe in line long after the device is off.

settings.label: First Use
settings.title: Pressure Eases
settings.text: Wear it for 15 minutes while the frame gently eases your big toe off the inflamed joint and the EMS starts working the muscle around it. Many people notice that hot, throbbing pressure soften in the very first session.

settings.label: Week 1–2
settings.title: Things Calm Down
settings.text: Redness and swelling around the joint start to settle. Steps feel softer, your usual shoes stop fighting you, and the night-time throbbing quietens so you can sleep.

settings.label: Week 3–4
settings.title: The Muscle Switches On
settings.text: The abductor hallucis, the muscle that holds your big toe straight, starts doing its job again. As it gets stronger, your toe sits straighter, stiffness eases and the correction begins to hold on its own.

settings.label: Week 5–9
settings.title: Feeling Like Yourself Again
settings.text: A few minutes a day keeps the muscle strong and the toe aligned. Flare-ups stop running your day, and the shoes you'd given up on come back into rotation.
